text:
Ian: FYI — noticed a repeat pattern this morning after we enabled the conservative-burst nodepool. Cluster Autoscaler is aggressively scale-downing preemptible GPU nodes in eu-west-1b and we end up with AZ skew (lots of GPU capacity concentrated in eu-west-1a). Training jobs are failing their AZ affinity checks.

Ian: snippet from CA log:

autoscaler: ScaleDown: removing node gpu-euw2-b-13 (nodeGroup: gpu-burst-euw2) reason: unneeded (no pods), utilization=0.06, podsEvicted=3

Ian: kubectl shows those pods were short-lived scoreboard-sidecars + a couple of pending daemonset eviction blockers (kube-proxy). PDBs look fine.

Maria: ugh. Two things to consider: AZ balance and the expander/weighting heuristics. Right now I think we're running expander=least-waste which tries to minimize leftover CPU/memory — that can punish GPU pools because they appear "wasteful" when they have a few pods.

Maria: quick proposals:
- bump --scale-down-unneeded-time to 20m (was 10m)
- set --scale-down-delay-after-add=15m to give burst nodes breathing room
- enable --balance-similar-node-groups=true so CA considers cross-AZ groups when choosing nodes to remove
- set --max-empty-bulk-delete to 2 (prevent rapid multi-node prunes)

Tyler: +1 on balance-similar-node-groups. We should also think about node-group weighting: if we tag the dedicated GPU pools with a higher priority (annotation/label CA understands) we can make CA prefer scaling down the burst/preemptible pool first.

Tyler: example approach: annotate nodegroups with cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/priority: "200" for dedicated, "50" for burst. Then use expander=priority (if we flip to that expander) to respect those priorities.

Sarah: Pod-side mitigation: make critical training jobs use PodPriority and a toleration for a protected taint on dedicated nodes. That will avoid accidental eviction by CA decisions and schedule them only on high-priority pools. Also set appropriate resource requests/limits — tiny requests on GPU pods confuse utilization math.

Ian: Good. Two other small CA flags I've seen help with GPU churn: --skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false (we want CA to consider nodes even if DS/LS present?) — currently it's true in our config and that has blocked some deletions, so maybe leave it. Also adjust --scale-down-utilization-threshold from 0.5 -> 0.65 to be less aggressive for big machines.

Maria: Right. For GPUs it's often better to raise the utilization threshold. A single GPU pod using 80% GPU but small CPU looks low-util on CA's CPU+mem calculation. We can also add custom metrics via CA webhook (future) to include GPU utilization in scale decisions.

Ian: Quick repro command I ran:

kubectl get nodes -l nodepool=gpu-burst-euw2 -o wide
kubectl describe node gpu-euw2-b-13 | egrep "Taint|Allocated|Non-terminated|Pods"

Autoscaler-bot: [event] scaleDownCandidate: gpu-euw2-b-13 (group: gpu-burst-euw2) at 2026-03-18T08:12:03Z reason=unneeded utilization=0.06

Tyler: Can we also throttle scale-down while a rollout or big job is running? There's --scale-down-disabled flag toggle but it's global; maybe implement a short-lived annotation on the cluster (or use the CA webhook) to temporarily pause scale-down when we detect a critical training window.

Sarah: For immediate mitigation let's do:
- [ ] bump scale-down-unneeded-time to 20m
- [ ] set scale-down-delay-after-add=15m
- [ ] enable balance-similar-node-groups=true
- [ ] add nodegroup priority annotations for dedicated vs burst pools
- [ ] increase scale-down-utilization-threshold to 0.65

Ian: I'll open a runbook PR for the above and schedule a short canary rollout to the eu-west cluster. Will also add a Grafana panel to show per-AZ GPU counts so we can alert on >20% AZ skew.

Maria: After canary, if we still see problems we should prototype a tiny CA fork (or use the priority expander) that takes GPU allocatable into account. I can spike a PoC next week.

autoscaler-bot: [info] cluster-autoscaler config updated by Ian — pending canary rollout (changes: scaleDownUnneededTime, scaleDownDelayAfterAdd, balanceSimilarNodeGroups, scaleDownUtilizationThreshold)

Ian: thanks — I'll post results in #eng-infra after the canary. :white_check_mark:
